analysis.title: Oil shock keeps Fed and bond markets guessing
key_insights: Government bonds rallied for a second straight week in a flight to quality as AI and technology stocks sold off, and the risk-off move spread beyond thematic names into more durable parts of the market.

Total returns followed duration. Municipals (+1.14%) and Treasuries (+0.56%) led, while preferreds (-0.39%), senior loans (-0.31%), high yield (-0.11%) and emerging markets (-0.08%) lost ground as spread widening outweighed lower yields.
Brent crude climbed to $117 per barrel, keeping energy-driven inflation concerns in view.
Nuveen expects the Fed to raise rates once more by year-end, then hold through 2027. This is less hawkish than market pricing and depends on how the energy shock passes through to core inflation.
Nuveen forecasts the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.95% for year-end 2026 and 4.75% for year-end 2027, and the 2-year at 4.70% and 4.50%.

Spread widening is concentrated in AI-linked and thematic credits rather than broad-based deterioration, though a second consecutive week of decompression could warrant closer attention. Credit fundamentals remain sound.

Treasury curve bull-flattened for a second straight week: the 2-year fell 2 bps to 4.68%, the 5-year 6 bps to 4.81%, the 10-year 8 bps to 5.00%, the 20-year 10 bps to 5.37% and the 30-year 10 bps to 5.32%. Rate volatility stayed elevated.
Political turmoil kept French bonds under pressure. French-German spreads widened midweek before retreating from their worst levels, and French banks and AT1 bonds repriced lower.

Municipals led for a second consecutive week. The index yields 4.31% and high yield municipals 5.90%. Nuveen favors longer-duration municipals over Treasuries and sees technical weakness as a chance to add high-quality duration.

Investment grade corporates saw liquidity narrow, a flatter credit curve as selling concentrated in shorter maturities, slower primary supply and a second week of fund inflows well below the four-week average.

High yield weakened midweek on the AI and data center selloff. Higher-beta AI, data center and neocloud names moved sharply in both directions, funding concerns in AI and telecom pushed cash prices lower on Thursday, and CCC credits lagged while higher-rated paper was roughly flat.
Senior loans deteriorated as lower-quality names came under pressure, loan ETF outflows amplified the move, and several deals were pulled from syndication.
Lower-rated CLO segments were the weakest performers. The CLO BB index returned -1.71% on the week, while high-quality CLO paper was well bid and roughly unchanged.
In securitized credit, agency MBS performed well (+0.75%), CMBS spreads widened and the AAA/BBB basis reached a year-to-date high, and ABS paused with a more cautious tone.
EM hard currency sovereign spreads widened in both investment grade and high yield, led by frontier credits. Retail outflows accelerated for a second week and new issue demand was below average.
The week ahead includes the FOMC meeting on October 28, ECB, PCE inflation, personal spending and Q3 GDP on October 29, BOJ and euro area Q3 GDP on October 30, and China PMI on October 31.
